subject: Odds ratios in a posterior parameter plot

messages.author: c621ac38989fbf3c
messages.subject: Odds ratios in a posterior parameter plot
parts:
Hey Paul,
 I've used the mcmc_intervals function in bayesplot to generate this figure. I'm trying to present the x axis in the most comprehensible way to my readers.

I think it's an effective graphic, but I'm not entirely clear on the units of the x axis. I am assuming it is logit scale, and it is change in log odds for each change in my parameters.

Is this something I can change into something more comprehensible to non-statistician readers, like an odds ratio?

messages.author: 6e3dd74b422c061b
messages.subject: Re: [brms-users] Odds ratios in a posterior parameter plot
parts:
I don't know exactly what kind of model you fitted, but I assume it is a binomial model, right?

You could try exponentiating the posterior samples of the coefficients to arrive at odds ratio changes and then pass the exponentiated samples to mcmc_interval.

messages.subject: Re: [brms-users] Odds ratios in a posterior parameter plot
parts:
Let me think about that. So lets say we have two predictors, one with coefficient 1 and one with coefficient 0 (logit-scale).

exp(param) would yield 2.7 and 1 in those two cases. Let's say both parameters have roughly the same distribution (just shifted by 1 in comparison).

However, exp(param - mean(param)) whould yield the same odds ratio for both coefficients, although the first clearly has a higher association with the response than the second. Does that makes sense?
2017-08-30 20:51 GMT+02:00 Paul Lantos <paul....@gmail.com>:

Because that would make it an odds ratio rather than just odds, right?
